Wound Care Instructions After Orthopedic Surgery

Proper wound care after orthopedic surgery reduces the risk of infection, promotes healing, and minimizes scarring. Follow these instructions carefully and contact your surgeon's office with any concerns.

Immediate Post-Discharge Period (Days 1–3):
Keep your surgical wound dry and covered with the dressing applied by the hospital nursing staff. Do not get the incision wet during this period. Avoid activities that cause sweating, as moisture under the dressing increases the risk of infection. Keep the dressing clean and change it as instructed — typically every 24 hours or whenever it becomes wet or soiled. Always wash your hands thoroughly before and after touching the wound or the dressing.

Shower Instructions:
You may shower after 48 hours post-discharge unless instructed otherwise. Cover the wound with a water-resistant dressing before showering if your staples or sutures are still in place. Avoid direct water spray on the incision. Pat the area dry gently with a clean towel after showering. Do not take baths, soak in hot tubs, swim in pools, or swim in natural bodies of water until your surgeon confirms the wound is fully healed — typically 4 to 6 weeks after surgery.

Dressing Changes:
Your surgeon's team will specify the type of dressing and how often to change it. General guidance: remove the old dressing carefully and discard it. Inspect the wound before applying the new dressing (see inspection guidelines below). Apply the new dressing as instructed. Secure it with medical tape if needed. If you are unsure how to perform a dressing change, ask a home health nurse or family member to assist.

Wound Inspection:
At each dressing change, inspect the wound for the following and contact your surgical team if you observe any of these:
- Increased redness: Some redness around the incision is normal in the first few days; redness that is spreading, worsening, or accompanied by warmth is concerning.
- Swelling: Mild swelling around the incision is expected; severe or worsening swelling is not.
- Drainage: A small amount of clear or light pink drainage in the first 24–48 hours is normal. Yellow, green, cloudy, or foul-smelling drainage is abnormal and requires evaluation.
- Wound separation: The edges of the incision should remain together. Any opening or separation requires prompt medical evaluation.
- Fever: A temperature above 101°F in conjunction with any wound changes requires immediate medical attention.

Staple and Suture Care:
Many orthopedic incisions are closed with surgical staples. These will be removed at your first post-operative visit (typically 10–14 days after surgery). Do not attempt to remove staples or sutures yourself. Keep the area around the staples dry and clean.

Scar Management (After Wound Healing):
Once your wound has fully closed (typically 4–6 weeks post-surgery), your surgeon may recommend scar management strategies to improve the appearance and flexibility of the scar. Options may include silicone gel sheets, scar massage, and sun protection. Discuss scar management with your surgical team once the wound is fully healed.

When to Seek Urgent Evaluation:
Go to the emergency room or call 911 if you experience: fever above 101°F with increasing wound redness, warmth, and drainage; wound edges pulling apart widely; very heavy drainage soaking through multiple dressings; or rapidly spreading redness extending beyond the wound margins.
